negative_findings.description: No vendor case study, press release or customer page was found in which a global core-banking vendor (Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Finastra/Misys, TCS BaNCS, Infosys Finacle) explicitly names a Kosovo bank as a customer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for core-banking go-lives returned only unrelated markets (Malawi, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kenya) and generic vendor-comparison listicles. The only attribution of Temenos T24 to a Kosovo bank (Raiffeisen Bank Kosova) comes from a paid technographics aggregator, not from the vendor.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The core-banking layer, the most strategically important, is precisely where vendor-side disclosure for Kosovo is weakest. Installed-base mapping for core will need bank-side and regulator-side evidence (annual reports, procurement notices, job ads naming platforms) rather than vendor pointers.

negative_findings.description: Halcom's public 'banks using Halcom' list, fetched directly, covers Serbia, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Albania and names no Kosovo bank, despite secondary search snippets suggesting Halcom entered the Kosovo market and that Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo was an early Halcom mobile-bank user.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fetched list contains four country groupings, none of them Kosovo. The Kosovo market-entry claim could not be corroborated on a primary vendor page in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Illustrates that vendor customer lists in this region are maintained per legal entity and can silently drop or never include Kosovo; absence from a logo wall must not be read as absence from the market. Archived snapshots are needed.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Serbian-language vendor communication about Kosovo appears to be effectively absent, probably for political/market reasons: regional vendors address the Kosovo market in Albanian or English. Serbian remains useful for Serbia-headquartered vendors' general reference lists (Comtrade, Asseco SEE Serbia, Halcom) but not as a Kosovo-specific channel.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor customer lists and case studies are routinely pruned; the current snapshot understates historical Kosovo wins (e.g. Comtrade's Kosovo references include institutions that no longer exist under those names, such as the Banking and Payments Authority of Kosovo and Kasabank).

coverage_gaps.description: The cell relies on vendors self-publishing, but the dominant pattern observed in Kosovo is that the vendor stays silent and evidence leaks through technical fingerprints (app package namespaces, e-banking URLs, certificate issuers) and local PR.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Formalise a fingerprinting collection routine as a first-class source class: app package ids and iOS sellers, e-banking hostnames and TLS certificate subjects, HTML/JS vendor markers on bank portals, and SWIFT/scheme BIN registrations.

brief: Vendor-side disclosure for Kosovo is thin but real, and it clusters at the edges of the stack rather than the core: ATM/POS and card processing are documented (Printec naming TEB and BPB ATM programmes, Compass Plus naming ProCredit Bank Kosovo's 2001 card project via Quipu, Quipu naming the ProCredit Kosovo mobile app and e-commerce gateway), while not one global core-banking vendor was found publicly naming a Kosovo bank. The highest-yield standing sources are regional vendors with Kosovo legal entities (Asseco SEE sh.p.k. Prishtina and Payten, Comtrade, Printec) plus the trade-press stream at FinTech Futures, which carried the one clean 'Kosovo institution selects vendor' item found (Cash Plus / Profile Software Finuevo). Because vendors often stay silent about this market, the most productive complements are technical fingerprints — Android package namespaces such as hr.asseco.android.jimba.nlbpr for NLB mKlik Kosova and com.quipugmbh.* for ProCredit — and Albanian-language corporate PR in national media, which is where wins like PriBank choosing IPKO for its banking infrastructure actually appeared. Serbian-language vendor communication about Kosovo is effectively absent, and AML and e-signature have no vendor-side Kosovo evidence at all.
